newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch Zalm concerned over German gold plan - paper.
newsitem.headline: Dutch Zalm concerned over German gold plan - paper.

text.p: A proposed plan to revalue Germany's gold reserves to reduce its government deficit was very disturbing, Dutch Finance Minister Gerrit Zalm told a Dutch evening newspaper on Thursday.

"It makes me worried that these kind of measures are being considered," Zalm said in an interview with the NRC Handelsblad. "I can't imagine that Germany wants to qualify for EMU, with regard to the budget deficit, in this way."

German Finance Minister Theo Waigel last week announced a plan to revalue central bank gold reserves nearer market prices as a way of meeting the deficit targets for qualification for the European single currency.
"Germany must meet the criteria in a proper manner," Zalm told the paper. "I can't imagine that Germany is prepared to put its reputation for soundness in the balance.
"I trust that Germany will reach the goal of a maximum three percent deficit in 1997, not through a one-off windfall from the Bundesbank, but rather by spending limits and increased tax revenues."

The NRC Handelsblad said Zalm, currently chairman of the European Council of Finance Ministers, planned to travel to Bonn soon to seek further details from Waigel. -- Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000, Fax +31 20 504 5040
